Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging. Let me tell you why it's so great. And the structure that I read about in these movies was different. In the movies, every movie starts with some kind of shift in the world, in the character's world. So he comes in and he says, "Hey, software is over," meaning software in the sense that we're going to own it and maintain it, "And there's this new world called the cloud, a new game, like the new rules, everything has changed and that's the new way to win. answer.summary: Raskin found the hero’s journey too theoretical to guide a pitch, and people tended to glaze over. Instead, he focused on the structure of one strategic story: explain a shift in the audience’s world and make the person you’re pitching the main character in responding to it.

sections.heading: What he considered a mistake
sections.content: Using the hero’s journey as a pitch template didn’t tell him what to do in practice. He found it too theoretical, and when he used it, people seemed to glaze over, so he stopped talking about it directly.

sections.heading: What he focused on instead
sections.content: Rather than storytelling as a general skill or a story about a separate hero being rescued, he focused on the structure of one story. It spells out a shift from an old game to a new game—such as Salesforce’s shift from owned software to the cloud—and turns the person being pitched into the main character who must adapt and can choose to come along.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately says the hero’s journey felt too theoretical to guide what to do in a pitch and that people seemed to glaze over. It also captures his alternative: focus on the structure of one clear story, with the person being pitched as its main character.
